Elizaphan
ē-lĭz´ă-făn
n. (chief of the Kohathites; also a prince of Zebulun)
Hebrew Elitsaphan, meaning God hath protected or hidden. Two men bear it — the Levite who carried the sanctuary's holiest furniture, and a tribal prince appointed to divide the land.

Biblical Definition

The Kohathites bore the ark, the table, the candlestick and the altars, and their chief is named: “And the chief of the house of the father of the families of the Kohathites shall be Elizaphan the son of Uzziel” (Numbers 3:30). This is the man Moses called, with his brother Mishael, to carry the bodies of Nadab and Abihu out of the camp after strange fire. A second Elizaphan is set over the division of Canaan: “And the prince of the tribe of the children of Zebulun, Elizaphan the son of Parnach” (Numbers 34:25). The Levite's house reappears when David brings the ark to Jerusalem the second time, by the due order: “Of the sons of Elizaphan; Shemaiah the chief, and his brethren two hundred” (1 Chronicles 15:8). And the reason David summoned these families rather than hiring a cart is stated in the same chapter: “Then David said, None ought to carry the ark of God but the Levites: for them hath the LORD chosen to carry the ark of God, and to minister unto him for ever” (1 Chronicles 15:2).

Webster 1828 Definition

Webster (1828) has no entry for Elizaphan; the Hebrew signifies God hath protected, and the name belongs to a Kohathite chief and to a prince of Zebulun.

expand to see more

ELIZAPHAN, n. The son of Uzziel, chief of the Kohathites; in Hebrew, God hath protected.

KOHATHITES, n. The family of Levites descended from Kohath, charged with the most holy furniture of the sanctuary.

BEAR, v.t. To carry; to support and remove from place to place; to convey.

STAVES, n. plu. The poles by which the ark and other sacred vessels were borne upon the shoulders.

SANCTUARY, n. A sacred place; the most retired and holy part of the temple or tabernacle.

Numbers 34:25 — "And the prince of the tribe of the children of Zebulun, Elizaphan the son of Parnach."

Modern Corruption

The care Scripture takes over who may handle holy things is treated as ritual fussiness, and David's own explanation of the breach at Perez-uzzah is passed over.

expand to see more

This entry faces no significant postmodern redefinition. The principle to recover is that God appointed both the thing to be done and the persons to do it. The Kohathites under Elizaphan carried the ark on staves upon their shoulders; they were forbidden to touch the holy things or even to look upon them uncovered, on pain of death. When David first moved the ark he used a new cart, which was the Philistine method, and Uzzah died. Three months later he summoned the Levites, and named the sons of Elizaphan among them, saying plainly that none ought to carry the ark of God but the Levites.

The lesson David drew is the sentence that gave the Reformed churches their doctrine of worship: we sought him not after the due order. The first attempt had every mark of sincerity — thirty thousand chosen men, singing, harps, psalteries, cymbals, and a brand-new cart. What it lacked was obedience to a command already given. The question Scripture puts to any act of worship is not whether it is heartfelt or impressive but whether it is commanded, and Elizaphan's sons on the day of the second attempt are the picture of the right answer.

Greek & Hebrew Roots

Hebrew Elitsaphan (H469), God hath protected; Qehath (H6955), Kohath; nasi (H5387), a prince; mishpat (H4941), due order.

expand to see more

Hebrew Elitsaphan (H469) — God hath protected; chief of the Kohathites.

Hebrew Uzziel (H5816) — his father, a son of Kohath.

Hebrew Qehath (H6955) — Kohath; the Levitical house that bore the holiest furniture.

Hebrew nasi (H5387) — a prince, chief; Elizaphan of Zebulun, Numbers 34:25.

Hebrew mishpat (H4941) — judgment, due order; the rule David had broken.

Usage

"“The chief…of the Kohathites shall be Elizaphan the son of Uzziel” — the appointment."

"“Of the sons of Elizaphan; Shemaiah the chief” — summoned for the ark."

"“None ought to carry the ark of God but the Levites” — David's correction."
